text.p: These are some of the leading stories in the official Iraqi press on Tuesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- President Saddam Hussein chairs joint meeting of the members of the regional command of the Arab Baath Party and members of the Revolutionary Command Council.
- Decision taken to send helicopters to transport pilgrims from the border with Saudi Arabia.
- Any American action threatening the safety of the helicopters and the pilgrims will be faced with proper reaction to deter aggression.
- Iraq and Greece hold talks to expand bilateral cooperation.
- A Dutch economic delegataion reviews cooperation with Iraq in Baghdad.
- Vice-President Taha Yassin Ramadan meets Malaysian foreign minister.
(The above were also carried by JUMHOURIYA and AL-IRAQ)
- Article on Saddam's role in enriching national thinking.
- Article on crime in the United States.
- Malaysian minister holds further meetings with Iraqi officials.
- Lebanese businessmen ready to invest in Iraq.
- Washington says all options against Iran are open.
- Article on Iran's attempts to export its revolution.
- Editorial backs Iraqi leaders' decision to send helicopters to southern Iraq and warns Washington against intercepting them.
